criteria.name: B1-1  a shared potential annihilates every cycle
criteria.detail: largest |cycle sum| over squares and a spanning basis, across 8 shapes: 8.88e-16. Theorem 1, (1) implies (3)

criteria.name: B1-2  the squares detect what no single agent can see
criteria.detail: 7/7 shapes where every w_a is exact but the potentials differ: slice cycles vanish below 1e-10, squares reach 4.272, and no global potential exists. A family of gradients need not be a gradient

criteria.name: B1-3  the path integral reconstructs the potential
criteria.detail: largest |d0 psi - omega| over every edge after integrating along a spanning tree: 8.88e-16. Theorem 1, (3) implies (2)

criteria.name: B1-4  the generating set spans the cycle space
criteria.detail: rank of the slice-plus-agent-plus-square matrix equals E - V + C on Gamma, for all 8 shapes. The two are computed by different code paths sharing nothing

criteria.name: B1-5  the closed form for the first Betti number is right
criteria.detail: m*e_G + n*e_H - m*n + 1 equals E - V + C for all 8 shapes: 2, 3, 16, 10, 39, 37, 26, 18

criteria.name: B1-7  one agent class reproduces the one-index case exactly
criteria.detail: at m=1 there are no squares at all and b1(Gamma) = b1(G). The enlarged graph is a generalisation, not a substitution

criteria.name: B1-8  the slice summand fires where the squares are silent
criteria.detail: 5/5 shapes with a shared but non-exact field: slice cycles reach 15.0 while every square sum is exactly 0.0. The mirror of B1-2, and the case every other field in this repository makes vacuous by construction

criteria.name: B1-9  on a mixture each summand comes back out unchanged
criteria.detail: 5/5 shapes: adding a pure-slice field to a pure-square one leaves both sets of cycle sums identical as raw bytes, slice reaching 15.0 and squares 22.0. Integer fields, so this is exactness and not a tolerance. Without it the split of Theorem 2 is checked on one summand and asserted on the other
